meta.task_prompt:
Implement GitHub issue #9 on this repo: "add redis caching in auth proxy for kanban endpoints."

There is already a shared Redis client at `internal/pkg/redis/main.go`, and it is
already used elsewhere in the codebase (see `internal/app/server.go` and
`internal/pkg/server/permissions/perm.go` for the existing usage pattern). Follow
that same pattern rather than inventing a new one.

Scope:
- Add caching for the read paths in `internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go`.
- Add cache invalidation on the corresponding write paths, so a write never
  leaves a stale cached read behind.
- Pick sane key naming and TTLs consistent with how the existing Redis usage in
  this repo does it.
- This repo currently has no test files. Do not feel obligated to introduce a
  whole test framework for this change, but do double check the code compiles
  and, if there's an easy way to sanity-check the caching behavior manually
  (e.g. a local run), do that.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly what
you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and body
verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal note.

code_review.summary: The read-through caching for GetLabel, getItem, exportKanban and getKanban copies the existing GetLabels/getItems pattern: GetItemFromRedis/AddItemToRedis, the X-cache: HIT header, 24h TTL and colon-separated keys. The item update/delete and createKanban invalidations are wired correctly, and the code compiles. Two problems block the merge. First, to make comment invalidation 'work', the PR makes a new `item_id` query parameter mandatory on PATCH and DELETE /kanban/comment and returns 400 when it is missing. No caller in the repo sends that parameter, so any existing client that edits or deletes comments stops working. Second, invalidation is still incomplete for the reads the PR newly caches. Comment writes never clear `<board>:export` or the `<board>:items:*` pages, and both embed comments. createLabel never clears `<board>:export` either. That misses the task's explicit rule that a write must never leave a stale cached read behind. Scoping the item cache under the board prefix and reusing `DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)` on comment writes, the same way item writes already do, would fix both problems without breaking the API.

findings.summary: UpdateComment and DeleteComment now return 400 unless callers send a new `item_id` query parameter that no existing client sends, which breaks editing and deleting comments.
findings.failure_scenario: The frontend currently calls `PATCH /kanban/comment?comment_id=X` or `DELETE /kanban/comment?comment_id=X`. Both the engine's reviewer and its coder confirmed that nothing in the repo sends item_id to these routes. Those calls now get `400 item_id is required` and the comment is never updated or deleted, so a user of the kanban board can no longer edit or remove comments until the client is changed. Also, the client supplies item_id and the server never checks it, so a wrong value still leaves the real `item:<id>` entry stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Don't make comment endpoints depend on a new client parameter. Key the item cache under the board, e.g. `boardId + ":item:" + id`, so the existing `DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)` already clears it. Then have AddComment, UpdateComment and DeleteComment call `redis.DeleteAllKeysPrefix(c.Request.Header.Get("X-Board"))` like createItem/updateItem/DeleteItem do. If you keep item_id, treat it as optional: use a targeted delete when it is present and fall back to the board-prefix delete when it isn't, never a 400.

findings.summary: Comment writes only clear `item:<id>`, so the newly cached `<board>:export` and the existing `<board>:items:*` pages, which embed comments, stay stale; createLabel likewise never clears `<board>:export`.
findings.failure_scenario: In kanban.proto, `Item.comments` is `repeated Comment` and `Board` holds items plus labels. A user adds a comment, then opens GET /kanban/items or GET /kanban/export. Both return the pre-comment snapshot from Redis for up to 24h. Similarly, after POST /kanban/label (which only deletes `<board>:Labels`), GET /kanban/export keeps serving an export without the new label. task.md explicitly requires that 'a write never leaves a stale cached read behind'.
findings.suggested_fix: In AddComment, UpdateComment and DeleteComment, call `redis.DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)`. It covers items pages, export, and (with board-scoped item keys) the item entry. In createLabel, also delete `board + ":export"`, or switch it to the board-prefix delete.

findings.summary: exportKanban caches an `ExportResponse{downloadLink}` for 24h, which assumes the generated link stays valid and current for a day.
findings.failure_scenario: If the kanban service returns a presigned or short-lived download URL, which is typical for exports backed by object storage, a cache HIT within the 24h window hands out an expired link. Export is also a user-triggered action where people expect fresh output, so caching it gains little.
findings.suggested_fix: Either leave exportKanban uncached, or confirm how long the link lives and use a TTL shorter than that (which needs a TTL-parameterised helper).

findings.summary: getKanban calls `redis.Rdb.Get/Set` directly and repeats the `1*86400*time.Second` TTL inline, instead of going through a helper in internal/pkg/redis like every other cached handler.
findings.failure_scenario: Everything else in routes goes through the redis package helpers. The route file now owns its own TTL constant and context handling, so a future TTL change in main.go will silently skip this key.
findings.suggested_fix: Add small `GetStringFromRedis(key) (string, bool)` / `AddStringToRedis(key, val string)` helpers next to GetItemFromRedis/AddItemToRedis in internal/pkg/redis/main.go that share the TTL. Call them here and drop the new `context`/`time` imports.

findings.summary: getItem and GetLabel build cache keys from query params without checking them, so a missing `id`/`label_id` caches the empty-id response under `item:`/`label:` for 24h.
findings.failure_scenario: A request missing `id` stores whatever the RPC returns for an empty id under `item:`. Later bad requests are served that entry, and nothing ever invalidates it.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 400 (or skip caching) when the id query param is empty, before building the cache key.

findings.summary: Nothing exercises the caching or invalidation behaviour: the only automated check is `go build && go vet`, and no manual run was attempted.
findings.failure_scenario: The engine's own mutation probe (flipping getKanban's `err == nil` to `err != nil`) still passed verification, so a broken hit/miss or invalidation path would ship unnoticed. The task said a new test framework wasn't required, so this is a note rather than a blocker.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider a small handler test with miniredis for one read/write pair (e.g. getItem followed by updateItem), or at least document a manual curl sequence checking X-cache before and after a write.

process_review.summary: For a single-file change of about 60 lines, the run cost $2.69, took 142 turns and 152 tool calls, and ran about 32 minutes of wall time across 7 subagents. The ask agent's survey was efficient and accurate: list_symbols, then targeted read_file and searches. The coder edited with proper read-before-edit and ran `go build` three times, all with ok: true. The overhead came from elsewhere. The orchestrator spawned a junk 'placeholder' ask agent. The first coder died on a malformed read_file call followed by a provider error. The second coder repeated many near-identical searches for item_id and comment. The first reviewer spent $0.97 and about 15 minutes, including tangents into reactions, README, swagger, invite tokens and board_id searches three times. The second reviewer was stopped by loop_control without giving a verdict. The PR was then opened while the orchestrator was still asking the user whether to re-review. The review loop did catch a real invalidation gap, but the orchestrator's fix brief listed 'make item_id required, 400 if missing' as a fallback. The coder took it without trying the board-prefix option the brief preferred, which swapped a silent staleness bug for an API break. No read-before-edit violations occurred. Judges mostly screened or ranked; write_gate flagged 12 times but was not enforced, and loop_control correctly stopped the stuck second reviewer.

findings.summary: The orchestrator spawned a second ask agent with the literal task 'placeholder' right after the real survey.
findings.evidence: Line 3: ask {"task": "placeholder"} started agent 5cd68480. The transcript says 'I made an accidental duplicate spawn there'. The agent reported 'No actual question or task was provided' ($0.016).

findings.summary: The first coder issued read_file with no arguments and then died on a provider error, so a retry agent had to redo all its reads.
findings.evidence: Line 32: read_file args {} -> 'error: read_file() missing 1 required positional argument: path'. The transcript then shows 'status: failed summary: error: Provider returned error'. The retry coder be9dfcc1 (line 34) re-read kanban.go in the same two windows (lines 38, 40, duplicating 27, 29) and re-ran the same RPC search (line 42 duplicates line 30).

findings.summary: The coder searched repeatedly for the same comment/item_id facts across the trace instead of settling the question once.
findings.evidence: Searches for 'Comment' (53), 'ItemId|itemId' (54), comment request structs (55), 'comment' in main.go (59), 'item_id' repo-wide (62), '/kanban/comment' (65), 'item_id|itemId|ItemId' in kanban.go (107), 'func.*Comment' (110), 'comment' in schema.sql (113), 'comment_id|item_id' in internal (115). All of these circle one question: does any caller supply an item id for comment routes?

findings.summary: The first reviewer was the most expensive agent ($0.97, about 15 min, over 50 tool calls) and drifted into tangents unrelated to reviewing a one-file diff.
findings.evidence: Reaction/reaction searches (184, 187, 188), README redis|cache (200), 'swagger|openapi|api.md|docs/' (204), invite-token/userAccount funcs (195), git_log (201), board_id searched three times (164, 194, 210), '/kanban/comment' twice (158, 166). The loop_control judge at line 196 reported repeating_itself 0.52 and making_progress 0.27.

findings.summary: The fix coder went straight to the brief's last-resort option (make item_id required, 400) without trying the preferred board-prefix invalidation, and dismissed it only because these handlers don't read X-Board yet.
findings.evidence: The orchestrator brief (line 213) preferred 'invalidate broadly ... redis.DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)' and made the 400 a fallback only 'if you truly cannot get any board or item id'. The coder's report says 'X-Board header is not read in these two handlers either, so a board-prefix fallback isn't available'. Reading a request header needs no new lookup. The coder then applied the 400 guard at lines 245 and 253, calling it 'the safest sub-variant', and itself noted that callers 'will now get a 400'.

findings.summary: loop_control stopped the second reviewer, which gave no verdict, and the PR was opened anyway while the orchestrator was still asking the user whether to re-review.
findings.evidence: Line 299 loop_control: making_progress 0.21, repeating_itself 0.69. stats show loop_control outcome stop_early=1. The reviewer returned 'status: stopped ... did not read the live file contents or diff'. The orchestrator's message contradicts itself ('I'll respawn a reviewer ... actually let me reconsider'), then it asks the user. Seconds later: '[worktree coder 298aacdc pr] opened pull request ... /pull/17'.

findings.summary: The compile check was done properly, but the manual sanity run the task suggested was never attempted; the coder claimed Redis wasn't available without running any command to check.
findings.evidence: run_command `go build ./...` at lines 120, 134 and 260 all show exit code 0 and ok: true. The coder report says 'no docker/redis-server confirmed running', but no run_command in the trace checks for redis-server or docker, or tries to start a local instance.

findings.summary: The second reviewer ran broad, low-value searches and git archaeology instead of just checking the two changed handlers.
findings.evidence: Searches for 'StatusBadRequest' (275) and then 'c\.String\(http\.StatusBadRequest' (277). A broad 'kanban\.|router\.|Router\.|POST|PATCH|DELETE|GET' search over internal/pkg/server (279). git_log/git_show of unrelated commit a26a0a1 (283 to 286). A second item_id search (290) that repeats earlier agents' finding.

strengths: The read-through caching copies the file's existing GetLabels/getItems pattern exactly: helpers, X-cache header, 24h TTL and key style.
Using raw Rdb.Get/Set for getKanban, which caches a plain string, was a reasoned choice, since GetItemFromRedis always unmarshals into a map.
Item update/delete and createKanban invalidations match their cache keys, and the export key is correctly covered by the board-prefix delete on item writes.
The build was verified with `go build ./...` (ok: true) after every change, and read-before-edit was respected throughout.
The engine's reviewer caught a real invalidation gap and the loop tried to fix it.
concerns: Requiring item_id on PATCH/DELETE /kanban/comment breaks existing clients, which the engine itself confirmed don't send it.

Comment writes still leave the cached `<board>:export` and `<board>:items:*` stale, and createLabel leaves `<board>:export` stale, which contradicts the task's 'never leave a stale cached read' requirement.
The PR was opened without a completed final review, and the process cost ($2.69, 7 agents, about 32 min) was out of proportion to a roughly 60-line single-file change.
overall_assessment.narrative: The caching half of this PR is solid and idiomatic for the repo. The invalidation half is where it falls short, and the process explains why. The review loop found a real gap, but the fix brief offered an API-breaking fallback, and the coder took it instead of reading an X-Board header and reusing the board-prefix delete that item writes already use. The final review was then cut off by loop_control and the PR went out anyway. Board-scoping the item cache key and calling DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board) on comment writes (plus clearing export on label creation) would make this mergeable. Until then it should not merge.
